title: IMF urges support for poorer nations facing high inflation, war spillovers
summary:

title: China’s economy grows 4.5 percent in Q3, beating forecasts
summary:
China’s economy has grown faster than expected in the most recent quarter amid booming exports underpinned by artificial intelligence, according to official figures.
During the first nine months of the year, GDP grew 4.6 percent year-on-year, according to the preliminary figures.
While China’s technology-related exports have surged during the AI boom, growth in the world’s second-largest economy has been dampened by weak domestic demand and a sagging property market.
China’s ruling Communist Party has set a GDP growth target of 4.5 to 5 percent for 2026, which would be among the slowest expansions in decades, excluding during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Americans earning over $500,000 are more likely to say they're living paycheck to paycheck than middle earners
summary:
Low and high earners have at least one thing in common: they're more likely than those somewhere in the middle to say they're living paycheck to paycheck.
A July survey of over Americans by Goldman Sachs Asset Management and behavioral economics firm Escalent showed about 61% of working respondents with less than $50,000 said they're primarily living paycheck to paycheck, meaning they struggle to save or make progress toward long-term goals.

title: Expansion of Heathrow Airport would drive growth, chancellor Healey says
summary:
Chancellor John Healey has said building a third runway at Heathrow Airport has "always been a case for growth" after Prime Minister Andy Burnham refused to say if he backed the expansion.
Healey said airport expansion, including at Heathrow, had been "a big part of jobs and growth" in recent decades, speaking at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Bangkok.
His comments came after Prime Minister Andy Burnham was more sceptical, telling the BBC last month it was "a matter for London and Londoners".
Healey's predecessor Rachel Reeves had put the airport's expansion at the centrepiece of an argument that Britain was open for business.
Healey told reporters: "The case for a third runway at Heathrow has always been a case for growth."
